ID3DXSprite::Draw may batch triangles until Flush/End. When the next canonical queue begins, the first 0x2D762 node arrives before QueueRenderActive is set, so previous transition admission based on an outgoing active queue missed a preceding direct result owner.

R64 now checks a live matched Begin/Draw sprite and homogeneous exact result producer, rebinds the saved producer across the old batch GPU Flush before selecting the first new node, and keeps the R84 ScreenHud finite per-eye plane unchanged.

diagnosis.root_cause: BeforeQueueNode only considered a transition when an existing queue owner was already active or the incoming node was an exact stage/GOAL source. A direct result batch still outstanding at the first unrelated queue node had no outgoing queue owner, so native D3DX implicit Flush could later submit under the newly selected producer.
diagnosis.source_evidence: R64 BeforeQueueNode is called before SelectSpriteQueueNode. QueueRenderActive is false for the first node, while tracked PendingScope/PendingProducer can still describe an original direct result Draw. The original pre-queue predicate admitted even an unknown None/None owner.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: R64 first-queue path checks exact live sprite identity, homogeneous nonzero batch and exact source token, flushes with ScopedExactProducerSemantic(saved scope/token) before queue switch, and quarantines failed Flush. Unknown None owner excluded in pre-queue guard.
diagnosis.runtime_limit: Original game and Quest3 VDXR headset not exercised in this execution. Automatic checks and build verification do not prove a single binocular +TIME.
